Performance Metrics for Imbalanced Classification

metrics.Rd

Metrics that are suitable for imbalanced and multi-class classification. All of them take the true classes y_true (a factor) and either the predicted classes y_pred or the predicted class probabilities y_prob. Use evaluate to calculate several metrics at once.

Usage

ACC(y_true, y_pred)

BACC(y_true, y_pred)

GMEAN(y_true, y_pred)

MCC(y_true, y_pred)

KAPPA(y_true, y_pred)

IAM(y_true, y_pred)

F1(y_true, y_pred, average = "auto", positive = NULL)

PRECISION(y_true, y_pred, average = "auto", positive = NULL)

RECALL(y_true, y_pred, average = "auto", positive = NULL)

SPECIFICITY(y_true, y_pred, average = "auto", positive = NULL)

P4(y_true, y_pred, average = "auto", positive = NULL)

ROCAUC(y_true, y_prob, average = "auto", positive = NULL)

PRAUC(y_true, y_prob, average = "auto", positive = NULL)

Brier(y_true, y_prob, positive = NULL)

PBrier(y_true, y_prob, positive = NULL)

BBrier(y_true, y_prob, positive = NULL)

ECE(y_true, y_prob, n_bins = 10, positive = NULL)

BECE(y_true, y_prob, n_bins = 10, positive = NULL)

LOGLOSS(y_true, y_prob, positive = NULL)

Arguments

y_true

factor of the true classes.

y_pred

predicted classes. A factor or a character vector with labels from the levels of y_true.

average

how class-wise values are combined for metrics that are defined for one class: "binary" uses only the positive class, "macro" is the mean over classes, "micro" pools the counts (or scores) of all classes, "weighted" is the mean weighted by class sizes. The default "auto" is "binary" for two classes and "macro" for more.

positive

the positive class of the binary versions. Default is the smallest class of y_true.

y_prob

predicted class probabilities: a matrix with one column per class (named after the levels of y_true, or in level order), or, for two classes, a vector with the probability of positive.

n_bins

number of equal width confidence bins of ECE and BECE. Default is 10.

Value

a number.

Details

Metrics based on predicted classes:

  • ACC: accuracy.

  • BACC: balanced accuracy, the mean recall over the classes.

  • GMEAN: geometric mean of the class recalls (for two classes \(\sqrt{sensitivity \cdot specificity}\)).

  • MCC: Matthews correlation coefficient, in the multi-class form of Gorodkin (2004).

  • KAPPA: Cohen's kappa.

  • IAM: imbalanced accuracy measure (Mortaz, 2020), in \([-1, 1]\).

  • F1, PRECISION, RECALL, SPECIFICITY, P4: class-wise metrics combined with average. P4 is the harmonic mean of precision, recall, specificity and negative predictive value (Sitarz, 2022). A class-wise value with an empty denominator is 0; classes that do not occur in y_true are ignored by "macro" and "weighted". Micro averaged F1, PRECISION and RECALL equal ACC.

Metrics based on probabilities:

  • ROCAUC: area under the ROC curve. Multi-class values are one-versus-rest and combined with average.

  • PRAUC: area under the precision-recall curve, calculated as average precision. Multi-class values are one-versus-rest and combined with average.

  • Brier: the Brier score, the mean over observations of the sum over classes of the squared differences between the probabilities and the one-hot true class. Lies in \([0, 2]\); for two classes it is twice the usual \((p - y)^2\) form.

  • PBrier: penalized Brier score (Ahmadian et al., 2024): the Brier score plus \((K-1)/K\) for every misclassified observation, which keeps a wrongly classified observation from scoring better than a correctly classified one.

  • BBrier: balanced Brier score, the mean of the class-wise Brier scores, so that every class counts equally.

  • ECE: expected calibration error of the predicted class (confidence), \(\sum_b (n_b/n) |acc_b - conf_b|\) over equal width confidence bins.

  • BECE: balanced expected calibration error, ECE where every observation is weighted by the inverse size of its true class.

  • LOGLOSS: logarithmic loss.

The probabilities of ECE, BECE, PBrier use the class with the highest probability as the predicted class.

References

Gorodkin, J. (2004). Comparing two K-category assignments by a K-category correlation coefficient. Computational Biology and Chemistry, 28(5-6), 367-374.

Mortaz, E. (2020). Imbalance accuracy metric for model selection in multi-class imbalance classification problems. Knowledge-Based Systems, 210, 106490.

Sitarz, M. (2022). Extending F1 metric, probabilistic approach. arXiv:2210.11997.

Ahmadian, S. et al. (2024). Superior scoring rules for probabilistic evaluation of single-label multi-class classification tasks. arXiv:2407.17697.

Examples

set.seed(1)
y_true <- factor(sample(c("a", "b", "c"), 100, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.7, 0.2, 0.1)))
prob <- matrix(runif(300), 100, 3, dimnames = list(NULL, levels(y_true)))
prob <- prob / rowSums(prob)
y_pred <- factor(levels(y_true)[max.col(prob)], levels = levels(y_true))
BACC(y_true, y_pred)
#> [1] 0.2183258
F1(y_true, y_pred, average = "micro")
#> [1] 0.3
MCC(y_true, y_pred)
#> [1] -0.05586563
ROCAUC(y_true, prob, average = "macro")
#> [1] 0.423633
Brier(y_true, prob)
#> [1] 0.7447057
